issues.body:
## Why

`src/counter_risk/parsers/cprs_ch.py:385-386` checks `"all" in title` before `"trend" in title` in `_detect_variant`. A Trend workbook copied to a filename containing both substrings (for example `mosers-trend-all.xlsx`) is classified as `all_programs` and fails with missing segments `futures_cdx, repo, swaps`. Verified: copying `tests/fixtures/CPRS-CH Fixture - Trend.xlsx` to `/tmp/mosers-trend-all.xlsx` raises that ValueError while the original filename parses successfully.

## Scope

Prevent spurious `all_programs` classification when the workbook content is Trend-only.

## Non-Goals

No change to segment validation rules for genuine all_programs workbooks. Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: reordering checks without a regression test is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/parsers/cprs_ch.py:381`, tighten `_detect_variant` so explicit `trend` markers win over incidental `all` substrings in generated filenames.
- [ ] In `tests/parsers/test_cprs_ch.py`, add `test_parse_cprs_ch_trend_workbook_not_misclassified_when_filename_contains_all` using a Trend fixture copied to an all-containing filename.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Named test: `tests/parsers/test_cprs_ch.py::test_parse_cprs_ch_trend_workbook_not_misclassified_when_filename_contains_all` parses the Trend fixture under an all-containing filename without missing-segment errors.
- Deliberate-break → revert: restore the current `"all" in title` precedence; the named test must fail; revert and confirm pass.
- `python -m pytest tests/parsers/test_cprs_ch.py::test_parse_cprs_ch_trend_workbook_not_misclassified_when_filename_contains_all -q` passes.

_Surfaced by Track D audit 2026-09-20; verified by parse_cprs_ch repro on tip 56bee4fa._
issues.title: [P2] Fix trend CPRS misclassification when filename contains spurious all

## Why

`src/counter_risk/pipeline/reconciliation.py:177-178` computes `missing_clearing_houses` with a raw set difference against historical headers, while counterparties use normalized matching at `:152-167`. Verified: clearing house `ICE` in parsed data against historical header `ICE Clear US` yields `missing_from_historical: ['ICE']` and `gap_count: 1` despite normalized equivalence available via `normalize_clearing_house` at `:184`.

## Scope

Apply clearing-house normalization when detecting missing historical headers, mirroring counterparty normalization.

## Non-Goals

No change to counterparty registry inclusion policy or fail/warn reconciliation modes. Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: normalizing only the data side without historical headers is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/pipeline/reconciliation.py:177`, compare normalized clearing-house labels from parsed data against normalized historical headers instead of raw string difference.
- [ ] In `tests/pipeline/test_reconciliation.py`, add `test_reconcile_clearing_house_canonical_label_does_not_false_flag_missing_from_historical` with ICE vs ICE Clear US fixture.

Repo-cash reconciliation warnings emitted from `src/counter_risk/pipeline/run.py:1232-1375` use structured codes such as duplicate counterparty names, but `src/counter_risk/pipeline/data_quality.py:506-547` auto-generates truncated codes via `_code_from_message` with `category: pipeline` instead of `cash`. issues.body:
## Why

`src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py:411-437` reads `notional_change` via bare `float(...)` without a finite guard, unlike `_find_numeric` used elsewhere. NaN propagates to `absolute_change` and breaks sort order in `top_changes`. Verified: `top_changes([{..., 'notional_change': float('nan')}])` yields `absolute_change: nan`.

## Scope

Apply the same finite numeric validation used by `_find_numeric` to `notional_change` and derived change values in `top_changes`.

## Non-Goals

No change to concentration metrics or pipeline exposure builders already guarded elsewhere. Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: documenting NaN behavior without raising is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/counter_risk/compute/rollups.py:414`, validate `notional_change` and derived change values with `math.isfinite` and raise `ValueError` on non-finite input.
- [ ] In `tests/compute/test_rollups.py`, add `test_top_changes_rejects_non_finite_notional_change` covering NaN and Infinity inputs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Named test: `tests/compute/test_rollups.py::test_top_changes_rejects_non_finite_notional_change` asserts `ValueError` for NaN `notional_change`.
- Deliberate-break → revert: remove the finite guard; the named test must fail; revert and confirm pass.
- `python -m pytest tests/compute/test_rollups.py::test_top_changes_rejects_non_finite_notional_change -q` passes.

_Surfaced by Track D audit 2026-09-20; verified by top_changes NaN repro on tip 56bee4fa._

## Why (verified evidence)
